editorial:
Imagine sitting around a table with a group of old friends who have known each other for over forty years. That is exactly what you get with this documentary. It follows the men of A-Company from the 4th Infantry Division who went through the whole Vietnam War experience together. You get to see their journey starting from basic training in 1965 all the way to their final reunion in 2007. The vibe is very personal and honest because you are hearing the stories directly from the soldiers. It is less about the politics of war and more about the brotherhood and the bonds these men formed while fighting for their lives.

What really makes this stand out is how the film focuses on First Sergeant David McNerney and his Medal of Honor. The pacing is steady, and while it is a bit slow at times, the raw emotion makes up for it. You will feel like you are part of the group. If you enjoy true stories about loyalty, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by focusing on the 2007 reunion in Houston, Texas. You see the surviving soldiers coming together one last time to honor David McNerney. It shows that even though they grew old and the world changed, their friendship stayed strong. The film ends with a feeling of peace and closure, proving that the love they had for each other was the only thing that truly lasted after the war ended.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about war and friendship.
